title: 11.4 A Gm-C RF Quadrature-Current-Generation Technique with 40dB IRR in 0.65V 2mW Multi-Mode CMOS GNSS Receiver
problem: Signal-quadrature receiver topologies offer power efficiency over LO-quadrature designs but suffer from poor I/Q phase and amplitude accuracy due to parasitic capacitances and impedances that are difficult to calibrate when using signal-engaged switches.
motivation: Ultra-low-power GNSS receivers enable wearable location-tracking devices; improving receiver power efficiency while maintaining I/Q accuracy enables longer battery life.
method: A Gm-C (transconductance-capacitive) RF quadrature-current-generation technique that derives orthogonal I and Q signals directly from the RF signal using transconductor circuits rather than passive switches. This approach reduces parasitic sensitivity and enables robust phase/amplitude balance calibration.
key_novelty: Gm-C based quadrature generation achieving 40 dB image-rejection ratio (IRR) in a signal-quadrature topology, eliminating phase/amplitude imbalance challenges of conventional switch-based quadrature approaches.
contributions: Gm-C quadrature-current-generation topology with reduced parasitic sensitivity
Robust phase and amplitude balance suitable for integrated calibration
40 dB IRR in multi-mode GNSS receiver (covering multiple GNSS standards)
Ultra-low-power implementation at 0.65 V supply, 2 mW total power
limitations: Sensitivity analysis across PVT variations, specific GNSS modes supported, and receiver sensitivity/noise figure not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-power Gm-C quadrature receiver for multi-mode GNSS applications
